clue.text: Escaping penalty if second bed unoccupied

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
a seat that is unoccupied is free

explanation.surface: A hotel guest dodges a charge on condition the second bed was never slept in.
explanation.definitionFit: To get off without punishment is to go unpunished, so the phrase describes escaping a penalty.

clue.text: City newly built, as last of seven

indicators.note: something built newly is put together afresh, so the letters are rearranged
the final letter of the word seven is taken

explanation.surface: A city has been rebuilt, the latest of seven such cities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'newly' rearranges BUILT, AS and N, the letter that 'last of' takes from 'seven'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Turkish metropolis on the Bosphorus is a famous example of a city.

clue.text: Stink over Queen Elizabeth I's bones

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece over another comes first

parts.note: to hum is British slang for to smell bad
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the royal cipher for Queen Elizabeth, followed by the numeral I

explanation.surface: A bad smell hangs over the remains of the Tudor monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: The upper-arm bones are each called a humerus, and this is the plural form.

clue.text: 9 of Beatlemania Abbey Road inspired, upsetting Merseyside initially

indicators.note: the opening letter of each of the six words from Beatlemania to Merseyside is taken

parts.words: Beatlemania Abbey Road inspired, upsetting Merseyside

explanation.surface: Fan fever, stirred up by an album, upsets Liverpool's home county.
explanation.walkthrough: 9 is the answer to 9-down, ELEMENT. Merseyside is the English county around Liverpool, home of the Beatles; Abbey Road is their album and studio.
explanation.definitionFit: This soft metal, atomic number 56, is a chemical member of the periodic table.

clue.text: Male members search carefully for pot plant

parts.note: cocks are male birds
to comb an area is to search it thoroughly

explanation.surface: Men in a club hunt carefully for a cannabis plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pot plant' suggests cannabis, but it is simply a houseplant grown in a pot.
explanation.definitionFit: Celosia, with its crested crimson flower heads, is a plant often grown in pots.

clue.text: Avant-garde barman's places behind bars

definitions.meaning: belonging to John Cage, the avant-garde composer, a man of musical bars
puts in an enclosure or prison, a verb

explanation.surface: An experimental bartender's spots are in prison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barman' looks like a pub worker but is a composer, whose music is written in bars.
explanation.definitionFit: To lock someone or something up behind bars is to confine it in an enclosure, a verb.

clue.text: Fibre from tree Greek character's going up

parts.note: the oak is a tree

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means read from the bottom, so backwards

parts.note: mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: Plant fibre comes from a tree as a Greek man climbs it.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose hemp or jute fibre picked from old rope is used to caulk ships' seams.

clue.text: Game time for a Saint

parts.note: bridge is a card game

explanation.surface: A game played in time for a saint's day.
explanation.definitionFit: St Bridget of Kildare is one of Ireland's patron saints.

clue.text: Handling what'll go in text for you: blue, short truncated version of 10

parts.words: what'll go in text for you
parts.note: U stands for 'you' in text messages

indicators.note: short means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: feeling blue is feeling sad

indicators.note: truncated means cut short, so the end of the first word of 10's answer is lost

parts.note: the first word of the answer to 10-across is Get

explanation.surface: Instructions on texting slang: sad feelings, and a shortened form of a song title.
explanation.walkthrough: 10-across is GET BACK; 'truncated version of' cuts its first word to GE, and 'short' cuts SAD to SA.
explanation.definitionFit: The way something is used or treated is its usage, so it means handling.

clue.text: Member of group lent me Beatle's last output

indicators.note: the final letter of the word Beatle
what lent me puts out is a new arrangement of its letters

explanation.surface: A band member lends the narrator the final release by a Beatle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Member of group' suggests a band player, but the group is a column of the periodic table. 'output' rearranges LENT ME, set after E, the last letter of Beatle.
explanation.definitionFit: Chemical substances in the periodic table are arranged in columns called groups.

clue.text: Retrieve some quite good content?

definitions.meaning: to retrieve something is to recover or regain it
a Beatles song on the album at 15, so a part of that album's fine contents

explanation.surface: Recover some decent material.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is the Beatles song, one track of the album LET IT BE at 15.
explanation.definitionFit: To recover what was lost is to regain it; the phrase is also a Beatles track title.

clue.text: Number of Eimi's first that's between a couple of Hob's

indicators.note: the letter goes between two pieces, so inside them

parts.note: Hob is the setter; read two ways, Hob's is 'I'm' (Hob is) and 'mine' (belonging to Hob)

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word Eimi

explanation.surface: A tune by a Greek friend sits between two of the setter's.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' is a song: George Harrison's track on Let It Be. 'Eimi' is Greek for 'I am', a sly hint at the song's subject.
explanation.definitionFit: A song is often called a number, and this is a Harrison song on the Beatles album.

clue.text: Axe crew found half-cut in warship

indicators.note: the shortened crew is placed in the warship, inside it

parts.note: a sub, submarine, is a warship

indicators.note: half of the word crew is cut away, keeping its first two letters

explanation.surface: A drunken sailor wielding an axe is discovered aboard a warship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-cut' is British slang for drunk, but here it halves CREW.
explanation.definitionFit: To axe a plan is to cancel it, and to scrub it is the same informal sense.

clue.text: Number one in game twice rearranged

indicators.note: the letters gathered are rearranged into a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: the word game is used twice

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A top-rated number in a game played twice, shuffled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twice' doubles GAME, and 'rearranged' scrambles those eight letters with I. The answer is a short Liverpool folk song on Let It Be.
explanation.definitionFit: A number is a song, and this traditional Liverpool ditty is a track on the Beatles album.

clue.text: Single number following IXOIX?

definitions.meaning: IX O IX in Roman numerals reads 909

explanation.walkthrough: IXOIX is nine, nought, nine in Roman numerals; the Let It Be song 'One After 909' makes the answer the number that follows it.
explanation.definitionFit: Being single means being unaccompanied, a sole individual.

clue.text: On rough terrain? Not on 15's long and winding track

parts.note: something not on is off
'The Long and Winding Road' is a track on the album at 15, Let It Be

explanation.surface: Driving rough country, off a long and winding route.
explanation.walkthrough: 'track' looks like a dirt path, but it is a song on the album; its last word supplies the piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A vehicle driven away from paved routes is travelling over rough ground.

clue.text: Album from Little Mix, one left out by editor initially

indicators.note: to mix letters is to jumble them up
out means removed from the word Little

parts.note: L is the standard abbreviation for left, and only one is removed

indicators.note: the opening letters of the words by and editor

explanation.surface: An album from the girl group Little Mix, with one track dropped by the editor.
explanation.walkthrough: Little Mix is a British girl group, but 'Mix' is the anagram signal. 'out' takes one L from LITTLE, leaving LITTE, and 'initially' gives B and E.
explanation.definitionFit: The Beatles' final released studio record is this title, an LP.

clue.text: First track setters, after tense outburst from one of them?

indicators.note: the setters' piece comes after the others

parts.note: T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense
setters are also dogs, and a dog's bark is woof
the setters, speaking of themselves, are us

explanation.surface: Crossword setters' first effort, after an anxious bark from one of their dogs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setters' is both the compilers, us, and the dog breed that barks.
explanation.definitionFit: This duet opens the Let It Be album, so it is its opening song.

clue.text: Lift veto Real violated

indicators.note: the words are violated, broken and abused, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Real Madrid broke a ban on lifting.
explanation.definitionFit: A lift is the British word for the car that carries people between floors.

clue.text: Fitting in Dig A Pony essentially, before end of set

indicators.note: the first piece comes before the second
the essence, the central letters, of the phrase Dig A Pony
the last letter of the word set

explanation.surface: A song fits into the set, played just before it ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dig A Pony' is a Let It Be song; the middle two of its eight letters are A and P.
explanation.definitionFit: Something apt is suitable or appropriate, just as fitting means.

clue.text: Adult with secret, first to be outed earlier

parts.note: A is the film-rating abbreviation for adult

indicators.note: the first letter of the word for secret is ejected

parts.note: interior means inner, private, hidden from view

explanation.surface: A grown-up with a hidden truth is the first to be outed.
explanation.definitionFit: Anterior means prior in time or position, coming before.

clue.text: Sweet little piano on which 10 played? That's sure to work

parts.note: a fool is a fruit-and-cream dessert, a sweet
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, soft
the Beatles played 'Get Back' in their rooftop concert on the Apple building's roof

explanation.surface: A cute little piano was played on, which is guaranteed to work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweet' in British usage is a dessert; a fool is one made of fruit and cream.
explanation.definitionFit: A method that cannot go wrong is infallible, so it is sure to succeed.

clue.text: Playing advantage, so I've got a feeling of nervous anticipation

definitions.text: I've got a feeling of nervous anticipation
definitions.note: the whole statement means 'I am tense'; the phrase is adjectival, describing that state

parts.note: a show that is playing is on
an edge is an advantage

explanation.surface: Playing with an advantage, I feel nervous anyway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I've Got a Feeling' is a Let It Be song, buried in the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Being tense and jittery with nervous anticipation is a state of being nervy.

clue.text: Very quickly forgetting name of 15's keyboard player

indicators.note: forgetting the name means its letter is dropped

parts.note: Billy Preston played keyboards on the Let It Be album

explanation.surface: The album's keyboard player quickly forgets a name.
explanation.definitionFit: In music, the tempo marking means at a rapid speed, and generally means instantly.

clue.text: Doctor starts to fly across the universe, lamenting poor service

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters are rearranged
the opening letter of each of the five words from fly to lamenting

explanation.surface: Doctor Who sets off to fly across the universe, bemoaning bad service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Across the Universe' is a Let It Be song. 'starts to' gives FATUL, which 'Doctor' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis, a serve that lands out is called by the umpire as an error.

clue.text: Consumed with envy originally, by a number having more than one 27

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word envy

parts.note: 27 is DIGIT, and ten is a number written with two digits

explanation.surface: Eaten up with envy by someone with several fingers.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that has been devoured has been swallowed up, so consumed.

clue.text: Wearing flesh colour, good for a jog

indicators.note: the colour wears the letter, so it goes round it

parts.note: nude is a flesh-coloured shade

explanation.surface: Someone out for a run in flesh-coloured kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a jog' looks like a run, but it is a gentle push.
explanation.definitionFit: A jog of the elbow is a gentle poke or push, a noun.

clue.text: Emphatically, the third person taking Ecstasy's being like Hob

parts.note: someone taking a drug is on it
E is the slang abbreviation for the drug Ecstasy, with the S of 's
a hob is a hobgoblin, an elf-like creature

explanation.surface: Someone high on Ecstasy behaves like the impish setter Hob.
explanation.definitionFit: The reflexive pronoun of 'one' is used for emphasis: one does it personally.

clue.text: Rain due — game not broadcast

indicators.note: game means willing to try anything, so the letters are ready to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Rain is due, so the match isn't shown on television.
explanation.walkthrough: 'game' looks like the match rained off, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A programme never shown on television or radio has never gone out on air.

clue.text: Number one from 15

definitions.meaning: any of the figures nought to nine
a short Beatles song on the album at 15, Let It Be

explanation.walkthrough: 'Dig It' is a brief jam on the Let It Be album.
explanation.definitionFit: Any single figure from nought to nine is a numeral.

clue.text: Having lowered the tone like this, poor Ovett heartlessly tormented Coe

parts.note: so means in this way

indicators.note: tormented, twisted about, says the letters are rearranged
the central letter of the word Ovett is removed

explanation.surface: Steve Ovett ruthlessly taunted Seb Coe, whispering in a low voice.
explanation.walkthrough: Ovett and Coe were rival British middle-distance runners. 'heartlessly' drops Ovett's middle E, and 'tormented' scrambles OVTT with COE.
explanation.definitionFit: This Italian musical direction means in an undertone, speaking softly and quietly.
